newsitem.title: USA: Flood damage in California estimated at $775 million.
newsitem.headline: Flood damage in California estimated at $775 million.

text.p: Floods that hit California have caused $775 million of damage in just nine counties and one city, according to initial estimates released by the state on Monday.

The figure does not include damage in some of the counties hardest hit by the flooding -- which have yet to estimate damage -- and the total is certain to rise, officials with the California Office of Emergency Services said.

The office said the early estimate already surpassed dollar damage figures from floods in 1955 and 1986. The winter storms of 1995, California's most damaging flood disaster in history, caused a total of $1.8 billion in damages.

The initial damage figure is based on reports filed by just nine northern California counties and the city of Morgan Hill, 70 kms (110 km) south of San Francisco. California Gov. Pete Wilson has declared a state of emergency due to flooding in 41 counties.
"Many of the most heavily affected areas of the storms were in central California and damage figures from those areas have yet to be reported," the Office of Emergency Services said.

Total damage to homes and businesses in the nine counties and one city was $242 million, the office said. Public property costs, including damage to infrastructure, such as roads and bridges, water and sewer systems, and government buildings, totalled $525 million, it said. It was not immediately known how the office accounted for the remaining $8 million.
